title: Mahanadi Coalfields Lists 1.47% Lower on Indian Stock Market
summary: Mahanadi Coalfields listed at ₹134 on the NSE, 1.47% below its ₹136 IPO price, as the Nifty 50 slipped and Waaree Renewable rose 10.2% on a solar order.
body_markdown:

*Regular-session close on November 25, 2026, New York time. Data: Massive.*


## How Much Demand Did the Mahanadi Coalfields IPO Get?


The Mahanadi Coalfields IPO was subscribed 1.52 times overall, according to[HDFC Sky](https://hdfcsky.com/news/mahanadi-coalfields-shares-list-at-rs-134-on-nse-1-47-percent-below-ipo-price) . The qualified institutional buyer portion, excluding anchor investors, was subscribed 4.95 times.


The other categories were each subscribed less than once. The non-institutional investor portion received 0.66 times subscription, the retail individual investor portion 0.46 times and the shareholder reservation 0.56 times, per HDFC Sky.


## How Did Mahanadi Coalfields Trade After Its ₹134 Listing?


The shares initially traded near ₹135 before declining towards ₹130, then recovered above ₹134, according to HDFC Sky. At 10:00 AM IST they were trading at ₹134.20, about 1.32% below the ₹136 issue price, with trading volume of 623,650 shares.


## Why Did Waaree Renewable Technologies Stock Jump 10.2%?


Waaree Renewable Technologies secured a Letter of Award for a 120 MWp turnkey solar power project covering the supply of solar modules and full engineering, procurement and construction works, according to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-waaree-renewable-technologies-stock-surging-today-93CH-5052953) . A domestic private limited company issued the award on the evening of November 26, after Thursday's market close, and the project is slated for completion in FY2027-28.


The stock traded from an open of ₹699.5 to a session high of ₹781.5, per Investing.com, which also noted a 285 MWp EPC work order signed earlier in November and a five-year operation and maintenance agreement covering 360 MWp. Investing.com described the award as a fully arm's-length transaction, with no promoter or group company interest in the awarding company.
